title: India's health system at a glance
standfirst: India can identify more than a billion people, insure the poorest 40% for hospitalisation, and screen at continental scale. It cannot tell you whether an abnormal result was ever followed up.

figures.label: of adults with hypertension have it controlled
figures.context: Roughly one in twelve. More than 90% are undiagnosed, untreated, or treated without reaching control.

figures.label: adults live with hypertension
figures.context: About 63% of them do not know it.

figures.label: adults live with diabetes
figures.context: Awareness ranges from 46% to 74% depending on how it is measured.

figures.label: national figures exist for referral completion after a positive screen
figures.context: Nothing in the published record answers it. The only measurements are two sub-district studies.

figures.label: hypertension screening events recorded
figures.context: Events, not people. Repeat screens are counted each time, so unique individuals are unknown.
figures.source: National NCD portal, Rajya Sabha reply

figures.label: of health spending is paid out of pocket
figures.context: PM-JAY covers hospitalisation. The outpatient care and medicines that chronic disease actually needs are not covered.

figures.label: per ABHA identity, on average
figures.context: 94 crore identities exist; 105 crore health records are linked to them across all of time.

figures.label: the last time India counted its population
figures.context: Every denominator here rests on projections. The domestic and UN estimates differ by about 50 million people.

vintageNote: This article is dated September 2026. Much of the data is not. The most recent national treatment-cascade measurements come from surveys fielded between 2017 and 2021, and there has been no census since 2011. Every figure above carries the period it actually describes.
